findings.reason: middleware/auth.ts:90 adds /_emdash/api/search to PUBLIC_API_EXACT, and search/index.ts:42 passes query.status to searchWithDb. query.ts:167 only defaults to 'published' when status is missing, and line 219 filters on the caller's value. So GET ?q=a&status=draft with no session returns drafts. The comment at auth.ts:87 saying the status is hardcoded is false.
findings.claim: The now-public search endpoint passes the caller's `status` through, so anyone without a login can read draft, scheduled or archived titles and snippets.
findings.evidence: middleware/auth.ts adds "/_emdash/api/search" to PUBLIC_API_EXACT, and search/index.ts drops `requirePerm(user, "search:read")`. The handler then calls `searchWithDb(emdash.db, query.q, { collections, status: query.status, ... })`. schemas/search.ts declares `status: z.string().optional()`, and search/query.ts:219 filters on `AND c.status = ${status}`. The FTS triggers in fts-manager.ts index every row whatever its status. So `GET /_emdash/api/search?q=a&status=draft` with no session returns draft titles and snippets. The comment added in middleware/auth.ts:87-89 says "The query layer hardcodes status='published'". That is untrue, and it would lead a reviewer to skip this path.

findings.reason: The diff adds a check at callback.ts:142-144 that returns Role.ADMIN whenever emdash:setup_complete is not true, before the allowed_domains lookup. Lines 191-192 then call finalizeSetup. /_emdash/api/auth/oauth/ is a public prefix (auth.ts:72), and nothing ties the callback to the setup wizard.
findings.claim: Before setup is complete, any GitHub/Google OAuth user becomes ADMIN and setup gets finalized, so a stranger can take over a fresh install.
findings.evidence: The new `canSelfSignup` returns `{ allowed: true, role: Role.ADMIN }` whenever `emdash:setup_complete` is not true, before the allowed-domain check runs. After `handleOAuthCallback` it calls `finalizeSetup(emdash.db)`, which sets `emdash:setup_complete`. `/_emdash/api/auth/oauth/` is in PUBLIC_API_PREFIXES, and nothing links the callback to the setup wizard. Trigger: on a new install with GitHub OAuth configured, an attacker opens /_emdash/api/auth/oauth/github and finishes the GitHub login. They become admin and setup is marked complete. Before this change, the domain allowlist gated signup at this point.

findings.reason: callback.ts:130-131 sets isFirstUser from the setup_complete flag alone. Line 138 uses setup_state.email and line 148 sets emailVerified, and lines 155-156 grant ADMIN. Nothing compares the DID with the handle stored in the wizard. login.ts has no setup-state check, so an attacker can start and finish OAuth first (an allowlist, if one is configured, would block this, but none exists by default).
findings.claim: Before setup is complete, whichever atproto DID finishes OAuth first becomes ADMIN with the owner's wizard email. The handle the owner entered is never checked.
findings.evidence: `isFirstUser = setupComplete !== true && setupComplete !== "true"`, and then `findOrCreateOAuthUser(..., async () => { if (isFirstUser) return { allowed: true, role: Role.ADMIN }; ...})`. setup-admin.ts stores `handle: body.handle` in setup_state, but callback.ts never compares it with `atprotoSession.did`. For the first user it sets `email = setupState?.email` and `emailVerified: isFirstUser`. login.ts (under the public prefix `/_emdash/api/auth/atproto/`) has no setup-state check. Trigger: the owner completes wizard step 1; an attacker POSTs `{handle:"attacker.bsky.social"}` to /_emdash/api/auth/atproto/login and completes OAuth. They become admin, finalizeSetup runs, and the owner's setup flow then fails with SETUP_COMPLETE.

findings.reason: callback.ts:130 reads the flag and only finalizeSetup at line 166 writes it, with no lock or conditional write between them. The core OAuth callback (lines 142/186-192) follows the same pattern. findOrCreateOAuthUser (consumer.ts:236-249) auto-links any verified email that already exists, so a second DID racing in with the setup email and emailVerified=true gets linked to the admin. The comments claiming this race is avoided are false. Lowered X1 from critical to medium: it needs two callbacks inside a narrow setup window, and C3 already covers the simpler takeover.
findings.claim: Checking the setup_complete flag doesn't prevent concurrent first-user callbacks. Both can create admins, or the second DID can be auto-linked to the admin through the shared wizard email.
findings.evidence: callback.ts:126 says "Using an option flag instead of countUsers() avoids a TOCTOU race where two concurrent callbacks both see 0 users and both create admins". But the flag is read with `options.get("emdash:setup_complete")` and only written later by `finalizeSetup`, with no lock or conditional write in between. The core OAuth callback ([provider]/callback.ts:140) has the same comment and the same read-then-write pattern. The comment at line 147 even says "safe if two callbacks race past the check".

findings.reason: login.ts:28, setup-admin.ts:56 and callback.ts:42 use url.origin, and client-metadata.ts:13 uses new URL(request.url).origin. None calls getPublicOrigin, which every core auth route in this change now uses for the siteUrl/reverse-proxy case. Behind a proxy, internal URLs such as http://localhost:4321 reach the PDS. Kept at medium (X2 said high): login fails outright, but it isn't a security breach.
findings.claim: The atproto routes build client_id and redirect_uri from the internal request origin instead of the configured public origin, so atproto login breaks behind a TLS-terminating proxy.
findings.evidence: login.ts, setup-admin.ts:56 and callback.ts:42 all use `const baseUrl = url.origin;`. client-metadata.ts uses `new URL(request.url).origin`. Every core auth route in the diff was switched to `getPublicOrigin(url, emdash?.config)` for exactly this reverse-proxy case (see public-url.ts). Behind a proxy, `http://localhost:4321/_emdash/api/auth/atproto/callback` would be registered as the redirect_uri.

findings.reason: integration/index.ts:210-217 sets security.checkOrigin: false for everything. checkPublicCsrf is only called at auth.ts:136 and :151, for public /_emdash API and plugin routes, so on-demand user pages and form POSTs outside /_emdash lose origin checking.
findings.claim: Astro's checkOrigin is turned off for the whole site, while EmDash's replacement CSRF check only covers its own public and plugin API routes.
findings.evidence: `const securityConfig = { checkOrigin: false, ... }; updateConfig({ security: securityConfig, ...})`. `checkPublicCsrf` is called only from middleware/auth.ts for `isPublicApiRoute` and `/_emdash/api/plugins/`. The other /_emdash routes need the X-EmDash-Request header. Template or user routes such as a contact-form POST no longer get any origin check. This weakens a secure default.

findings.reason: context.ts:496 adds `if (pattern === "*") return true`. The restricted client (lines 525-534) only calls isHostAllowed before globalThis.fetch, while the unrestricted client calls validateExternalUrl on every hop (line 579). So the wildcard grants more than network:fetch:any does.
findings.claim: A plugin with allowedHosts "*" can fetch any host, including private IPs and metadata endpoints, with no SSRF validation.
findings.evidence: `isHostAllowed` gains `if (pattern === "*") return true;`. `createHttpAccess` only calls `isHostAllowed` and then `globalThis.fetch(currentUrl, ...)`. `createUnrestrictedHttpAccess` (the fetch:any path) calls `validateExternalUrl(currentUrl)` on every hop. Trigger: a plugin with `allowedHosts: ["*"]` calls `ctx.http.fetch("http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/")`, and the request goes through.

findings.reason: login.ts sets no cookie or session marker, and callback.ts:60 accepts any state the server-side store knows, then sets the session at line 185. So nothing ties the state to the browser. Impact is limited to logging a victim into an attacker account that already exists, and whether the atcute library adds its own binding isn't visible here.
findings.claim: The atproto callback accepts any valid state/code without tying it to the browser that started the flow, which allows login CSRF.
findings.evidence: login.ts returns the authorize URL and sets no cookie or session marker. The OAuth state is held only server-side in the `auth:atproto` `states` collection (db-store.ts). callback.ts calls `client.callback(url.searchParams)` and then `session.set("user", { id: user.id })`, with no check that ties the state to the current session.

findings.reason: lunaria.yml:4 and :13 set pull_request_target and pull-requests: write, and line 29 uses lunariajs/action@v1-prerelease. Lines 20-24 pin every other action by SHA. If that tag moved, new code would run with a write token.
findings.claim: A pull_request_target workflow with pull-requests: write runs a third-party action pinned to a mutable prerelease tag.
findings.evidence: `- uses: lunariajs/action@v1-prerelease` under `on: pull_request_target` with `permissions: pull-requests: write`. In the same diff, other actions use pinned SHAs (e.g. `actions/checkout@de0fac2e...`).

findings.reason: The diff adds "@lunariajs/core": "https://pkg.pr.new/.../@lunariajs/core@83617cc" with a tarball resolution in pnpm-lock.yaml, and it is installed in the pull_request_target job. It is pinned to a commit and no exploit path is traced, so I lowered it to low as supply-chain hygiene.
findings.claim: A root devDependency installs from a pkg.pr.new preview build, not a published release.
findings.evidence: `"@lunariajs/core": "https://pkg.pr.new/lunariajs/lunaria/@lunariajs/core@83617cc"`, with a matching tarball resolution in pnpm-lock.yaml:3007. i18n/build.ts and lunaria.config.ts import it.

findings.reason: In the diff, sitemap-[collection].xml.ts still uses `settings.url || url.origin`, while sitemap.xml.ts and robots.txt.ts were switched to getPublicOrigin. Behind a proxy with no settings.url, the child sitemaps list internal URLs.
findings.claim: Per-collection sitemaps still use the internal request origin, while the sitemap index and robots.txt use the public origin.
findings.evidence: sitemap-[collection].xml.ts: `const siteUrl = (settings.url || url.origin)`. sitemap.xml.ts and robots.txt.ts in the same diff use `settings.url || getPublicOrigin(url, emdash?.config)`.

findings.reason: The diff deletes requirePerm(user, "search:read") from suggest.ts, and the suggest path isn't in PUBLIC_API_EXACT, so a login is still required but no permission is checked. getSuggestions hardcodes status='published' (query.ts:294), so the exposure is small.
findings.claim: The search:read permission check was removed from the non-public suggest endpoint.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes `const denied = requirePerm(user, "search:read"); if (denied) return denied;` from suggest.ts. `/_emdash/api/search/suggest` is not added to PUBLIC_API_EXACT, so middleware still requires a login, but nothing checks the permission any more.

findings.reason: csp.ts now emits "img-src 'self' https: data: blob:" instead of the marketplace-limited list. The changeset documents this as deliberate, but it does allow image beacons to any origin.
findings.claim: The admin CSP's img-src is widened to any https origin.
findings.evidence: `"img-src 'self' https: data: blob:"` replaces the earlier `buildEmDashCsp(marketplaceUrl)`, which allowed only 'self', data:, blob: and the marketplace origin.

findings.reason: 034_published_at_index.ts:13 has no IF NOT EXISTS. The 033 change in this diff, recorded in the changelog as a fix for 'index already exists', shows the project has already hit this failure mode.
findings.claim: The new migration 034 uses a bare CREATE INDEX, while 033 was patched to IF NOT EXISTS for idempotency.
findings.evidence: 034: `CREATE INDEX ${sql.ref(`idx_${table.name}_deleted_published_id`)}`. 033 was edited in this diff from `CREATE INDEX` to `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` for every index. Editing the already-shipped migration 033 also changes history that existing databases have already run.

findings.reason: The final stage, from FROM node:22-slim (line 37) to CMD (line 49), has no USER directive.
findings.claim: The runtime image runs the Node server as root.
findings.evidence: The final stage `FROM node:22-slim` ... `CMD ["node", "./dist/server/entry.mjs"]` has no `USER` directive, so the server and the writable `data`/`uploads` directories are owned by root.

findings.reason: That entry is the release history for #225, when the option was added. The same diff adds a later entry (diff.patch:486/492) saying siteUrl replaces passkeyPublicOrigin and that passkeyPublicOrigin is removed, so the changelog is accurate.
findings.claim: The changelog documents a non-existent passkeyPublicOrigin option.
findings.evidence: The CHANGELOG entry says "Adds `passkeyPublicOrigin` on `emdash()`". runtime.ts:294 says siteUrl "Replaces `passkeyPublicOrigin`", and no code reads `passkeyPublicOrigin`.

findings.reason: No *.test.ts file under packages/auth-atproto references routes/callback, isFirstUser or setup_complete. The first-user admin grant, the allowlist and disabled-user handling are all untested.
findings.claim: The security-critical atproto callback and login routes have no tests.
findings.evidence: The tests added for auth-atproto are auth.test.ts (descriptor shape), oauth-client.test.ts and resolve-handle.test.ts. None of them exercise routes/callback.ts or routes/login.ts.
